description: Clinical trials conduct, pharmaceutical/medical-device regulation, health data, and genetic privacy. Includes both harmonised international standards adopted as law (ICH) and jurisdiction-specific regimes.

regulatory_bodies.name: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency

regulations.name: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice
regulations.summary: International ethical and scientific quality standard for clinical trial design, conduct, recording, and reporting. R3 (2023) emphasises risk-proportionate quality, data integrity, and a principles-based approach.
key_requirements: Ethical conduct per Declaration of Helsinki
Informed consent of trial subjects
Scientific validity of trial design
Data integrity — ALCOA+
Quality by design and risk-based quality management
Sponsor and investigator responsibilities
Audit trails for all regulated records

regulations.name: EU Clinical Trials Regulation
regulations.summary: Harmonised EU framework for clinical trials, centred on the Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS). Mandatory from January 2023 for new trials.
key_requirements: Single CTIS application for all Member States concerned
Transparency — trial data published in CTIS
Coordinated assessment with a Reporting Member State
Informed consent aligned with GCP and Member State law
Protocol amendments via CTIS
Centralised safety reporting (SUSARs, Annual Safety Reports)

regulations.name: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
regulations.extra_territorial_scope: Applies to any organisation submitting to FDA or holding FDA-regulated records, regardless of location.
regulations.summary: FDA requirements for electronic records and signatures to be equivalent to paper and handwritten signatures.
key_requirements: Validated systems ensuring accuracy, reliability, consistent performance
Secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails capturing create/modify/delete
Record retention per predicate rule; retrievable for inspection
Access controls limited to authorised individuals
Electronic signatures with identity verification and non-repudiation
System documentation control

regulations.name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
regulations.summary: US law for Protected Health Information. Also appears in data-protection.json as DP-US-HIPAA (same regulation — listed here for clinical/health context).
key_requirements: Privacy Rule — uses and disclosures of PHI; individual rights
Security Rule — safeguards for ePHI
Breach Notification Rule
Business Associate Agreements
Minimum necessary standard

regulations.name: Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act
regulations.summary: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of genetic information in health insurance and employment. Also appears in data-protection.json (DP-US-GINA).
key_requirements: Health insurers must not use genetic information for coverage / premium decisions
Employers must not use genetic information in employment decisions
Restrictions on requesting / requiring / purchasing genetic information
Confidentiality of genetic information where lawfully held
